phase1.explanation:
🦀 **if let and while let provide concise pattern matching.**

**if let:**
| Syntax | Use |
|--------|-----|
| `if let Some(x) = opt { ... }` | Handle one case |
| `if let Ok(x) = result { ... }` | Handle success |
| `if let Pattern = value { ... }` | Any pattern |

**while let:**
| Syntax | Use |
|--------|-----|
| `while let Some(x) = iter.next() { ... }` | Loop over values |
| `while let Ok(x) = reader.read() { ... }` | Loop until error |

**Rust-chan says:**
"if let is for when you only care about one pattern. Use it for conciseness."

**When to use if let:**
| Situation | Use if let |
|-----------|-----------|
| One pattern | ✅ |
| Two patterns | `if let ... else` |
| Many patterns | Use match |
| Looping over values | Use while let |
